chunks: Faḍālah ibn Sīnān, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Bashīr al-Nabbāl, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) saying:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) addressed the grave of Saʿd, and he would wipe it with his hand, and he would quiver between his shoulders. So it was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, we see you addressing [the grave] and quivering between your shoulders, and you say: Saʿd is undergoing this [squeezing]. So he said: Verily, there is no believer but that he will undergo squeezing [in the grave].

key_terms.بَيْنَ كَتِفَيْهِ: Between the shoulders, the specific location of the Prophet's quivering.
key_terms.ضَمَّةٌ: The squeezing or compression of the grave, a form of chastisement in the intermediate realm.
key_terms.قَبْرَ سَعْدٍ: The grave of Saʿd, the specific grave addressed in the narration.
key_terms.يَخْتَلِجُ: To quiver, tremble, or move restlessly, specifically referring to the Prophet's physical reaction.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet's quivering between his shoulders when visiting a grave?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the concept of *al-Dammah* (the squeezing of the grave) as a universal experience for all believers, not just the wicked, distinguishing it from the more severe *Nadl* (expansion) or specific punishments. The physical reaction of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) serves as a profound sign (*ayah*) of the reality of the Barzakh, reinforcing the Shia belief in the tangible nature of the intermediate realm.
